eligibility.evidence: Methods (Set-up and Data Collection; Community Analysis): observational network analysis of about 24,000 GPT-3.5 character bots on Chirper.ai; the outcome is community structure and assortativity, not responses to an administered cognitive task. Homophily is cited from sociology (McPherson et al., 2001), not as a laboratory paradigm. A reviewer could treat it as social cognition.

A.title: Artificial Intelligence Chatbots Mimic Human Collective Behaviour (indexed title: Homophily in An Artificial Social Network of Agents Powered By Large Language Models)

G.notes: Excluded: no cognitive-experimental paradigm; field observation of a deployed bot platform, model mostly GPT-3.5 without a snapshot. Borderline on social cognition. First author is in a psychology department at Cambridge (corresponding-author line); the file shows v2 (2024) of a 2023 v1. Data on OSF.
